# Admin service (`admin/src`)

The admin service is a single Bun + Hono process (package `@app-vitals/agent-admin`)
that owns the platform's control plane: agent records and their env vars, cron
jobs, tools, tokens, plugins and templates (ATP-1.1); self-serve accounts; provisioning of the
Kubernetes workloads behind each agent; a server-rendered admin UI; and the
runtime API deployed agents call to fetch their own config. State lives in its
own Postgres database (Prisma, `admin/prisma/schema/`).

Canonical sources are not repeated here:

- HTTP contract: `admin/openapi.json` (composed) and `admin/openapi.platform.json`
  (platform only), built from `admin/src/admin-spec.ts` and `admin/src/openapi-schemas.ts`.
- Data model: `admin/prisma/schema/schema.prisma` (platform models) and
  `admin/prisma/schema/coding.prisma` (coding-extension models); migrations in `admin/prisma/migrations/`.
- Auth and bearer scopes: [agent-api.md](agent-api.md).
- Chat service architecture and API: [chat-service.md](chat-service.md).
- Env var quick reference and Docker usage: `admin/README.md`.

## Module map

All paths are under `admin/src/`. Most modules have sibling `*.unit.test.ts`,
`*.integration.test.ts` and/or `*.smoke.test.ts` files.

### Boot and composition

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `main.ts` | Composition root. Exports `adminExtensions` (empty for the plain platform) and calls `startAdmin()` only when run as the entry point. Downstream images replace it to pass their own extensions. |
| `admin-boot.ts` | `startAdmin(extensions)`: the whole boot sequence (see "Boot order"). Process wiring only; must not import coding modules. |
| `admin-boot-config.ts` | Pure/env-driven helpers used by boot: `runMigrations`, `buildProvisioner`, agent-image-map parsing (`parseAgentImageMap`), pod-label parsing (`parseAgentPodLabels` from `agent-pod-labels.ts`), Anthropic federation parsing, `buildDeletionClients`, `checkDbReady`, sweeper interval resolvers, `DEFAULT_PORT`. |
| `admin-extension.ts` | The `AdminExtension` seam: optional hooks `serviceIntegrations`, `specialtyDefaults(name)` (default crons/tools/plugins, consulted by the cron reconcile and create-time seeding before the built-in specialist type, which stays the fallback), `agentTypes()` (agent types this extension offers, merged over the built-in types), `services` (its `openWork?: OpenWorkPort` seam feeds the GitHub reconcile; the last supplier wins, none means nothing is listed or blocked), `apiRoutes`, `adminUiRoutes`, `agentDetailCards`, `backgroundPasses`, plus static `openApi()`. Hook order is `ADMIN_EXTENSION_HOOK_ORDER`. |
| `service-integration.ts` | Interface for per-agent service integrations (token mint/revoke, Secret key, URL/token env) supplied by extensions; chat-service stays built in. |
| `server.ts` | Package entry (`exports["."]`): re-exports app factories, services, error classes and clients. It does not start a server. |
| `self-serve-config.ts` | Parses `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_*` into `{enabled, defaultMaxAgents, contactEmail}`. |
| `agent-ask-config.ts` | Parses `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED` and the `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST` `from>to` pairs into `{enabled, allowlist}`; a malformed pair throws. |
| `startup-policy-reconcile.ts` | One-shot, never-throwing policy-only reconcile of managed agents after `Bun.serve`. Also reconciles configured pod labels. Also exports `managedReconcileTargets`, shared with `POST /agents/reconcile`. |
| `prisma-client.ts`, `prisma-tx.ts`, `clock.ts`, `errors.ts` | Prisma 7 driver-adapter client (pool observability hook), optional-transaction param type, injectable `Clock`, typed `ApiError` subclasses. |
| `crypto.ts`, `token-crypto.ts` | AES-256-GCM (`iv:ciphertext:authTag`, hex). `makeTokenCrypto()` reads `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; unset means identity functions (plaintext). `makeStrictTokenCrypto()` is a strict variant that requires the key and throws on any decryption failure (no plain-text fallback), used for credentials that must never be stored unencrypted. |
| `github-enterprise-apps.ts` | `GitHubEnterpriseAppService`: platform-level GitHub Enterprise Apps (at most one per role: `installer` or `lookup`), optional feature. Private keys are encrypted (AES-256-GCM via `TokenCrypto`) and never returned by read paths. `save()` requires `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to be configured. |
| `github-enterprise-client.ts`, `github-app-jwt.ts` | `GithubEnterpriseClient`: signs an RS256 App JWT (`node:crypto`), mints the enterprise installation token, lists installable orgs and org installations, installs an App on an org, and manages repository access on an installation (list, add, remove, toggle all/selected), with typed errors (401/403/404/422/429/5xx/network). Setup, permissions and the isolation exception are in [github-enterprise-apps.md](./github-enterprise-apps.md). |
| `github-enterprise-api.ts`, `github-app-api.ts` | Admin-only `/github-enterprise` routes (GHE-1.3), mounted in `admin-boot.ts` and folded into the platform spec: `GET /github-enterprise/apps` (status: metadata plus `keySet` per role, `configured:false` when empty), `PUT`/`DELETE /github-enterprise/apps/{role}`, `POST /github-enterprise/apps/{role}/validate` (mints a token through `GithubEnterpriseClient`, or `GET /app` for `lookup`, checks the required permission, persists the result, and returns `{ ok, error, warnings }`; warnings are advisory non-failing notes about missing optional permissions), `GET /github-enterprise/orgs[?agentId=]` (installable orgs, with lookup-App and agent-App installed flags; includes `agentAppReason` when called with `agentId=`), `POST /github-enterprise/orgs/{org}/install` (uses the agent's stored `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID` when set and well-formed, otherwise resolves the stored `GH_APP_SLUG` through the public `GET /apps/{slug}`; 422 for an agent with neither a client id nor a slug, or for a private App with no stored client id). GitHub failures map to distinct non-leaky statuses (403 -> 424, 404, 422, 429 + Retry-After, 5xx -> 502, network -> 504). This is the only admin code that calls GitHub with App credentials; `github-enterprise-isolation.unit.test.ts` pins that the key never reaches the config bundle, agent-bearer routes or env serialization. |
| `admin-ui-github-enterprise.ts`, `admin-ui-github-enterprise-pages.ts` | Admin-only settings page `/admin/settings/github-enterprise` (GHE-1.4), registered when `createAdminUIApp` gets `githubEnterpriseApi` (the GHE-1.3 app's `request`; wired in `admin-boot.ts`). Installer and lookup cards (paste-only credentials form, validate and delete, status line: configured, key set, last validation result and time, and any advisory warnings) and an org list with install actions. Every action calls the GHE-1.3 routes with the caller's session cookie and shows their typed `{ error }` as a readable message; the private key is never rendered. The nav "Settings" entry is shown to admins only (`runWithSettingsNav`). The lookup App has no install route, so its action links to the App's GitHub install page. |
| `github-username.ts`, `github-lookup-client.ts`, `user-repo-access-resolver.ts`, `github-access-preview.ts` | GitHub username binding and access preview (GHE-2.1 to 2.4). `Agent.githubUsername` is set only through `PATCH /agents/:id` by a platform admin (syntax-validated in `github-username.ts`, stored lower-cased). `GithubLookupClient` reads org tokens, repos and collaborator permission through the lookup App; `UserRepoAccessResolver` combines them into a completeness-aware result (unknown is never none); `GET /agents/:id/github-access` returns it through the `GithubAccessPreview` port. The UI is `admin-ui-github-identity-pages.ts`. See [github-username-binding.md](./github-username-binding.md). |
| `repo-access-rules.ts` | Pure rules shared by Sync: `accessSkipReason` (no bound user, unresolved access, user not found or unverified skips the whole call), `orgSkipReason` (an org whose listing is missing, partial or failed, or whose lookup App is selected-only, is skipped: unknown is never none), `repoOrg`, `OrgSkip`. No I/O. |
| `installation-ports.ts`, `reconcile-open-work.ts` | `installation-ports.ts` holds the ports and adapters behind the installation repos service and Sync: `InstallationAgentsPort` (agent record with its own `GH_APP_ID`), `AppInstallationPort` and `createInstallationPort` (list/add/remove scoped to the agent App's installation on an org, found by `matchInstallation` via client id, then slug, then `GH_APP_ID`, since the enterprise endpoint omits `app_id`; `AppNotInstalledError` names the org), `InstallationAuditPort` and the Prisma adapters (`PrismaInstallationAgents`, `PrismaInstallationAudit` writing `GitHubReconcileAudit` rows), plus `MAX_UNCONFIRMED_REMOVALS` and `MISSING_APP_ID_REASON`. `reconcile-open-work.ts` is the `OpenWorkPort` seam: a consumer like shipwright may supply it so work on repos removed from an agent gets listed and blocked; with no port nothing is listed or blocked and a port failure is a warning. |
| `github-installation-wiring.ts` | `createGithubInstallationRepos` and `createGithubSync` compose the installation repos and Sync services for admin boot from the stored installer App and the extension's optional `OpenWorkPort`. The agent App is resolved per agent from its stored `GH_APP_ID`. |
| `installation-repos-service.ts` | IRM-1.2: `InstallationReposService` lists the repos on an agent's own App installation (admin-only `GET /agents/{id}/github-installation/repos`), with the `userPushHints` per-repo hint. Wired by `createGithubInstallationRepos` in `github-installation-wiring.ts`. |
| `github-sync.ts` | IRM-3.1: `planGithubSync` (pure, reusing `repo-access-rules.ts`'s `accessSkipReason` / `orgSkipReason`) and `GithubSyncService`, behind the admin-only `/agents/{id}/github-sync/{preview,apply}` routes: installation adds, installation removes and agent-repo removes for the bound user's push access (agent repos are never added to), one audit row (`GitHubReconcileAudit`, `sync:apply`), then open work blocked via `blockRepoRemovalWork`. Wired by `createGithubSync` in `github-installation-wiring.ts`. |
| `admin-ui-installation-repos-pages.ts` | IRM-1.4, IRM-3.2: Admin UI for the GitHub Sync card — the read-only list of repos on an agent's GitHub App installation per org, with `userCanPush` hints, and one Sync button that opens a single confirm step for installation adds, installation removes, agent-repo removes and the open work they block. Rendered on the agent detail page only for platform admins and only when both the installer and lookup Apps are configured; the button is replaced by a reason when the agent has no `GH_APP_ID` or no bound username, and a `GH_APP_ID` mismatch message shows when no installation matches. There is no add box. Exported types: `InstallationReposView`, `RepoRemovalPreviewView`, `OpenWorkView`. Also exports `renderUncoveredBadge()` and `uncoveredRepos()` (coverage warning for repos on the configured scope but not yet on the installation). Every dynamic value is escaped; inputs carry repo names and ids only. |

### Agent records and configuration services

`agents.ts` (`AgentService`), `agent-envs.ts` (encrypted env bundle; applies the
Anthropic credential guard), `agent-cron-jobs.ts`, `agent-tools.ts`,
`agent-tokens.ts`, `agent-plugins.ts`, `agent-members.ts`,
`agent-anthropic-identity.ts` (owner and Anthropic identity columns),
`anthropic-credential-guard.ts` (with federation on, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`,
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` must not reach federated agents),
`specialty-types.ts` (`SpecialtyTypes`, resolves a stored specialty to the built-in `specialist` record from `lib/specialist-type.ts`: tools floor, required env; the default type name is resolved by `lib/default-specialty.ts`).

### Provisioning and deletion

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `agent-provisioner.ts` | `AgentProvisioner` with `KubernetesAgentProvisioner` and `NoopAgentProvisioner`. Order: token, Secret, Deployment (PVC first; in perAgent identity mode also a K8s ServiceAccount, Anthropic service account and federation rule, with IDs saved as they are created so retries reuse them). Also `reconcile` and `deprovision`. |
| `agent-image-map.ts` | Per-specialty Docker image resolution (SPI-1.1): `parseAgentImageMap()` parses the `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGES` JSON map; `resolveImage()` returns the image for a given specialty (its own map entry, a `default` entry, or the single-image fallback). Interfaces: `AgentImageMap`, `AgentImageRef`. |
| `agent-manifest.ts` | Pure builders for the Deployment, token Secret and RFC1123 names. Merges configured pod labels (`agent-pod-labels.ts`) into the pod template. |
| `kubernetes-client.ts` | First-party fetch client for the in-cluster API (Deployments, Secrets, PVCs, ServiceAccounts); no `@kubernetes/client-node`. |
| `agent-deletion.ts`, `agent-deletion-checklist.ts` | `deleteAgentFully()`, shared by `DELETE /agents/:id` and the UI danger zone: deprovision, remove per-agent Anthropic identity, revoke extension tokens, revoke chat tokens and delete threads, optional Slack app delete; the Agent row is deleted last so retries work. Hand-pasted secrets become a manual-steps checklist. |
| `account-agent-create.ts`, `agent-account-assignment.ts` | Self-serve create rules (resolved self-serve specialty via `getSelfServeSpecialty()`, stamped with the caller's account, quota checked); reconcile a single agent after account (re)assignment via `reconcileAgentAfterAccountChange()` or after specialty change via `reconcileAgentAfterSpecialtyChange()` (SAL-1.2). |
| `github-provisioning-service.ts`, `slack-provisioning-service.ts` | Connect an existing agent to GitHub (App manifest flow or PAT) or Slack (app manifest + OAuth); used by the UI. |

### Accounts, invites and trials

`accounts.ts` (`AccountService`), `account-members.ts` (email-unique; last owner
cannot be removed or demoted), `account-invites.ts`, `account-onboarding.ts`
(first login joins the inviting account as member or creates one as owner, in one
transaction), `account-lifecycle.ts` (status transitions to cron lockdown and
restore, shared by the API, UI and sweeper), `account-email.ts`,
`account-created-notifier.ts` (best-effort push or log). Sweepers:
`trial-expiry-warning-sweeper.ts` and `trial-expiry-sweeper.ts` (per agent),
`account-trial-warning-sweeper.ts` and `account-trial-expiry-sweeper.ts` (per
account). Expiry disables crons only; nothing is deprovisioned.

### Web Push

`push-service.ts` (targets users via `ChatThreadWatch`, prunes 404/410
subscriptions), `push-sender.ts` (injected `fetch`, VAPID JWT), `push-crypto.ts`
(hand-rolled RFC 8291/8292 on `node:crypto`), `push-content.ts` (content policy
`generic` < `title` < `preview`, capped by the operator ceiling), `push-toggle.ts`
(thread-page toggle; renders `""` when push is off), `admin-ui-push-test.ts`
(`POST /admin/push/test`).

### Admin UI

Server-rendered HTML, no client framework. `admin-ui.ts` (`createAdminUIApp`:
login/OAuth, agents, provisioning, chat, session cookie `admin_session`) with
route modules `admin-ui-account.ts` (`/admin/account`) and `admin-ui-accounts.ts`
(`/admin/accounts`, platform admin). Rendering is pure string functions in
`admin-ui-pages.ts`, `admin-ui-account-pages.ts`, `admin-ui-accounts-pages.ts`,
`admin-ui-github-identity-pages.ts` (GHE-2.5 GitHub username and access preview),
`admin-ui-layout.ts`, `admin-ui-styles.ts`; `admin-ui-account-nav.ts` carries a
per-request nav flag. `pwa.ts` builds the manifest and service worker (austere
caching: nothing authenticated is cached); icons come from `admin/pwa-assets/`.
`theme-tokens.json` holds the design tokens. `chat-markers.ts` and
`attachment-validation.ts` support the chat pages.

### Fixtures and tests

`fixtures/` holds recorded HTTP cassettes (k8s, Okta, Google, Slack, GitHub App,

`*.fixtures.ts` files (`admin-ui`, `anthropic-identity-client`,

## Boot order

`startAdmin()` runs: Sentry init, `prisma migrate deploy` (skipped with a log if
`DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN` is unset), Prisma client, services,
`collectServiceIntegrations`, provisioner, extension resolution, routes, sweepers,
extension background passes, `Bun.serve`, graceful shutdown, then the startup
policy reconcile (fire and forget). The order is pinned by
`admin-boot.boot-order.unit.test.ts`.

Route mount order matters because both the runtime and admin apps live under
`/agents`:

1. `GET /health` (liveness, no DB) and `GET /health/ready` (`SELECT 1`; 503 once shutdown starts); `/` redirects to `/admin/login`.
2. Runtime API at `/agents` (`:id/config`, `:id/crons`).
3. Admin CRUD API, then `/accounts`, then extension API routes.
4. Admin UI at `/admin/*`, then extension UI routes.

Sweepers start after the routes: per-agent warning (hourly) and expiry
(`SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`) always; the account pair only
when self-serve is enabled. They are registered in `admin-boot.ts`, never inside
an app factory.

## Key data flows

- **Agent create and provision:** `POST /agents` (or the UI form) writes the Agent row; `POST /agents/{id}/provision` has the provisioner mint a scoped token, create the Secret and Deployment, plus extension-integration and chat-service tokens. With `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_PROVISIONING` not `enabled`, the provisioner is a no-op.
- **Agent config fetch:** a running agent calls `GET /agents/:id/config` with its bearer token; the runtime app returns the decrypted env bundle, plugins, marketplaces, repos and author allowlists.
- **Delete:** `deleteAgentFully()` as described above; a failed step leaves the row so the call can be retried.
- **Self-serve login:** OAuth callback, verified-email and allowlist/membership check, `AccountOnboardingService` (join or create account), session JWT cookie. Account is resolved per request, not stored in the JWT.
- **Trial expiry:** warning sweeper posts to the agent's Slack alert channel; expiry sweeper disables enabled crons (stamping `lockdownDisabledAt`); account suspend/reactivate goes through `AccountLifecycle`.
- **Push:** chat reply, `PushService.sendToUsers` to subscriptions of thread watchers, encrypted and VAPID-signed by `PushSender`.

## Configuration

Read at startup in `admin-boot.ts` and `admin-boot-config.ts`. Highlights; see
`admin/README.md` for the base table.

| Area | Variables |
|---|---|
| Core | `DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN`, `PORT` (3000), `SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_SECRET`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_APP_BASE_URL`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TZ` (validated; invalid exits), `SENTRY_DSN` |
| Login | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `OKTA_ISSUER/CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET` (Okta only when issuer set), `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS`, `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH` |
| Self-serve | `SHIPWRIGHT_SELF_SERVE_ENABLED=enabled`, `_DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS`, `_CONTACT_EMAIL`, `_AGENT_TYPE` |
| Cron run-now | `SHIPWRIGHT_CRON_RUN_NOW_ENABLED=enabled` (404 when off) |
| Agent ask | `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED=enabled`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST` (`from>to` pairs; empty denies all, malformed throws at boot); also needs the chat service vars |
| Transcripts | `SHIPWRIGHT_TRANSCRIPT_API_ENABLED=enabled` (cron-run transcript routes; also sets `features.transcriptUpload` in the config bundle; `SHIPWRIGHT_LOOP_TRANSCRIPT_AGENT_IDS` lists agents that also get `features.loopTranscriptUpload`) |
| K8s provisioning | `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_PROVISIONING=enabled`, `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_NAMESPACE`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE`/`_IMAGE_TAG`/`_REPLICAS`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGES` (optional JSON map of specialty to `{repository, tag}`; unmapped specialties and a `default` key fall back to the single image; malformed throws at boot)/`_PVC_*`, `SHIPWRIGHT_API_URL`, `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_*` (resources, service account, Claude policy configmap/hash) |
| Anthropic federation | `SHIPWRIGHT_K8S_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_*` (identity mode `shared` or `perAgent`; partial config throws at boot); admin pod's own sign-in via `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID` |
| Chat service | `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL` and `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_ADMIN_TOKEN` (both needed; otherwise chat pages degrade and deletion uses a no-op client) |
| Push | `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`/`_PRIVATE_KEY`/`_SUBJECT` (all three or push is off), `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_MAX_DETAIL`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` |
| Sweepers | `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS` |

## Run and test

```bash
bun install
cd admin && bunx prisma migrate deploy --schema=prisma/schema   # or let boot do it
bun run admin/src/main.ts                                       # from repo root, port 3000
```

Tests (repo root): `bun run test` (sets `NODE_ENV=test`; `scripts/test-env-preload.ts`
points specialties at a fixture). Integration tests need Postgres via
`DATABASE_URL_ADMIN_TEST` (CI also sets `DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN`).
`cd admin && bun run typecheck` for types; `bun run test:e2e` runs the Playwright
suite in `admin/e2e/` against a local server on port 3490. Docker:
`docker build -f admin/Dockerfile -t shipwright-admin .` from the repo root.

`admin-spec.ts` references `scripts/generate-admin-spec.ts` as the generator of
the composed `openapi.json`; that script is not present in this repo tree, so
check where the spec is regenerated before editing routes.
